mainEntity.name: What is the difference between drywall finish levels 1 through 5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drywall finish levels range from Level 0 to Level 5, established by trade associations to define surface smoothness before decoration. Level 1 involves basic tape embedded in joint compound, commonly used in concealed service corridors or attics. Level 2 adds a thin coat over tape and fastener heads, typical for garage utility areas or under tile. Level 3 includes an additional coat suited for heavy wall textures. Level 4 is standard residential construction, receiving two coats over joints and designed for light textures or flat paints. Level 5 applies a skim coat over the entire surface, which is necessary to prevent joint flashing under high-gloss paint or intense directional lighting.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drywall finish levels range from 0 (unfinished boards) to 5 (a full skim coat). Levels 3 and 4 support textured or flat finishes, while Level 5 prevents visible seams under glossy paint.
